rationale: Record the drift-then-snapshot receipt and move the snapshot question to violated. With the drifted state sampled first (accepted 9, 9, 6 and decided 9 on the three nodes) and the leader holding six indices of content, the public snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, advanced the compacted index to 8, and the snapshot the leader now serves for index 0 holds zero entry ids - none of the five decided entries the log contained - while the leader's own accepted index stayed 6 and its decided index 9. So a documented snapshot call, given an index inside the drifted decided index (which the note 'only up to the decided_idx can be snapshotted' allows), silently discarded the configuration's decided entries from the reader's view. A behaviour records that the snapshot bound and the snapshot range come from the drifted values, the interpretation becomes violated/asserted with the counterevidence and limits made explicit, and the parent question's drift now has two witnessed consumers that compact past the content.

knowledge.statement: On a leader whose decided index has drifted above its content, the snapshot path accepts a user-supplied index inside that drifted decided index, advances the compacted index to it, and builds the snapshot from a storage range that starts at the previous compacted index; when that range lies past the entries the log holds, the storage returns nothing and the snapshot is created from an empty slice, so the entries are no longer reachable through the log and the snapshot that now represents the region holds none of them.
knowledge.conditions: Snapshot-capable entry type (Snapshot::use_snapshots() true) with a snapshot that records its input entries; three-node cluster after a decided StopSign, three reconnection rounds giving decided 9 over six indices of content, then snapshot(Some(8), false) on the leader. Observed in receipt e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c: before the call the nodes reported accepted 9, 9 and 6 with decided 9 (events 0-2); the call returned Ok with compacted index 8, leader accepted 6 and decided 9, and the snapshot reachable at index 0 held 0 entry ids (event 3); afterwards the two drifted nodes reported accepted and decided 9 (events 4, 5).

interpretations.rationale: Witnessed: the snapshot path compacts and snapshots past the entries the leader holds, and the snapshot it produces holds none of them. Receipt e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c: after the drift the three nodes reported accepted 9, 9 and 6 with decided 9 while the leader held six indices of content (events 0-2); the public snapshot(Some(8), false) returned Ok, the leader's compacted index became 8, its accepted index stayed 6 and its decided index 9, and the snapshot served for index 0 held zero entry ids where the log had five decided entries (event 3). The declared comparisons requiring the compacted index to stay at the six indices of content and the snapshot to hold the five entries were both violated at that event, and the comparison requiring the call to be accepted was recorded unknown only because its admission chain shared an event name with another case in the same execution, while the operand shows the call returned Ok. Mechanism: try_snapshot bounds the request by the leader's decided index (internal_storage.rs 432-453) and the documented note permits exactly that (mod.rs 180-184), while create_snapshot builds the snapshot from the range starting at the current compacted index (internal_storage.rs 367-383); the drift lifts the decided index above the content, and the in-memory storage returns nothing for a range that does not exist (memory_storage.rs 92-107), so the snapshot is built from an empty slice while the compacted index passes the entries. The entries are no longer reachable through the log and the snapshot that now represents them is empty, which for an application that keeps its state in the snapshot means the state it compacted away is silently gone; the trigger is a caller-visible index the documentation describes as allowed, so the responsibility sits with the target's bound and range derivation rather than with the caller.
counterevidence: The call itself returned Ok, so nothing in its result signals the loss; the witness is the compacted index together with the number of entries the produced snapshot holds.

The user supplied the index 8; the documented note allows any index up to the decided index, and the decided index was 9, so the request was inside the documented allowance rather than a caller error.

In the sampled drifted state the StopSign adjustment of the equal case lowered the effective bound, so a request equal to the decided index is not the case that produced this witness; the witness used a strictly lower index.
limitations: The consequence depends on the entry type's snapshot: here the snapshot records its input entries and is empty for an empty slice; an entry type that reconstructs state differently could behave differently.

The snapshot was requested with local_only false in the call, so peers receive the forwarded compaction request; their own compactions were not sampled here beyond the accepted and decided indexes of events 4 and 5.
One three-node configuration, three reconnection rounds, one index and one entry type were exercised; other sizes, rounds and indexes were not.

The comparisons that would have tied the before and after samples to their admissions are unknown because of a shared event name in the same execution; the states are asserted from the sampled operands (events 0-5).
interpretations.joint_history: Same harness lineage as the drift account: receipt e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c ran experiment a9cad483efbe4868a0d1c52a13253499-experiment, whose snap case reproduces the events of receipt fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 and whose new case uses the same snapshot-capable entry type and the same three reconnection rounds as the trim receipt ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a; each case is read on its own samples and no measurement is combined across executions.

knowledge.assertion: the snapshot bound comes from the decided index alone
the recorded accepted and decided indexes drift one index per re-synchronization round

investigations.discriminator: Whether the same loss occurs for a snapshot request equal to the drifted decided index, for a request on a follower, or for an entry type whose snapshot does not derive from the entries themselves; and whether the peers that receive the forwarded compaction end in a different state than the leader.
